summary: Procurement and security review for Redwood onboarding. Customer wants MSA redlines, DPA clarity on data residency and KMS, cost comparison Hosted vs Dedicated including egress/reserved capacity, and an in-VPC benchmark for KV/prefix caching. Agreed next steps and owners.
topics: Pricing: Hosted vs Dedicated and egress fees
transcript:
[00:00] Sarah Mitchell: Hi everyone, thanks for joining. We scheduled this to move through the legal and procurement asks and make sure procurement has what they need to route pricing and SLA approvals. I see Lena, Priya, Mark, Omar on the call. Can you confirm?
[00:12] Lena Ortiz: Yep, Lena here. Thanks. This is basically the procurement intake, we want to validate the MSA exceptions, DPA, and understand any on-prem or VPC requirements. Also need a clear cost delta for Dedicated.
[00:25] Sarah: Great, Carlos is our SE and will talk about the Dedicated pieces and the performance tradeoffs. Carlos?
[00:31] Carlos Vega: Hey all. Quick note, Dedicated = reserved GPU pools, predictable throughput, lower unit cost for steady state. Hosted is fastest to start but can spike cost with large token volume and egress. We also support Redwood Private for VPC/private control plane.
[00:48] Mark Tanaka: On the security side, our main asks: KMS integration with customer-managed keys, audit logs that show token-level access, and SSO with SAML/SCIM for RBAC. Also question about data residency for EU traffic.
[01:05] Sarah: Understood. On KMS, we support KMS/HSM integrations - we can do customer-managed keys in Private deployments; for Hosted we have envelope encryption and can add bring-your-own-key via a partner KMS flow. We'll share the technical note.
[01:19] Priya Desai: For the DPA, the legal team needs clarity on subprocessors and international transfers. We had a clause request about deletion and retention windows for logs and prompt data.
[01:31] Sarah: We'll send a DPA variant that enumerates subprocessors and an option to restrict data residency. Carlos, can you explain how logs/audit behave across Dedicated vs Hosted?
[01:39] Carlos: Sure. In Dedicated and Private you can get full audit logs and control log retention; in Hosted we retain request metadata for X days by default but we can extend with an add-on. Note, sometimes transcripts have redactions; automatic PII redaction can be applied but that's part of the data retention dialogue.
[01:57] Omar Rahman: On billing, procurement wants the 'all-in' run-rate. Egress is a big unknown. How do you usually model egress and reserved capacity fees?
[02:08] Carlos: We model three scenarios: baseline Hosted with on-demand tokens + egress per GB; Dedicated with reserved GPU commit and an egress allowance; and Dedicated + burst with overage. We'll produce a spreadsheet. Important to model sequence lengths and KV cache hit rates because that drives token consumption.
[02:28] Lena: Procurement also needs the MSA redline. Our legal team will want to see indemnities, liability caps, and security attachments.
[02:36] Sarah: We'll push a redline. Quick call-out: Redwood offers SLA tiers for Dedicated that are contract-backed. Hosted SLAs are different and more usage-tier based. We'll include the SLA matrix.
[02:49] Priya: Any compliance reports? SOC 2? ISO?
[02:52] Sarah: Yes SOC 2 Type II available, ISO 27001 in progress. I'll attach the SOC 2 report and the security overview.
[03:00] Mark: For the Private deployment, where does the control plane live? If it's customer-managed, does Redwood still have access to telemetry?
[03:07] Carlos: In Private, control plane is customer-managed, networked in your VPC. We can configure telemetry to push to your logging endpoint; Redwood engineering access is tightly scoped and on a need basis with audit trails.
[03:20] Priya: The DPA language around subprocessors—do you list cloud providers and any infra partners?
[03:25] Sarah: We'll provide the subprocessor list. If there's a required addendum for a particular partner, we can mark it in the redline.
[03:31] Lena: Procurement needs timeline. We have a procurement board on 2026-05-18. Can we get required docs by 2026-05-11 so we can route?
[03:40] Sarah: Yes, we'll prioritize. We'll aim to send the redline and SOC 2 by 2026-05-10. Carlos will send the cost spreadsheet by 2026-05-12.
[03:49] Mark: We also want a short technical benchmark in our staging VPC to see KV cache behavior and latency at our sequence lengths. Can Redwood run a one-hour run inside our VPC?
[03:59] Carlos: We can. For Private or Dedicated, we can run a staged benchmark. We'll need a sample traffic profile, API keys scoped for the test, and an ingress slot. Nina from CSM will coordinate.
[04:13] Nina Park: I'll set up a 1-hour slot next week and send the invite.
[04:17] Priya: For procurement attachments, we need the final PO language and any escrow/termination clauses upfront. Any standard language you recommend?
[04:27] Sarah: We'll include standard PO templates and highlight where MSA controls the terms. If you need alternative termination liability caps for enterprise deals, we can discuss commercial exceptions with our legal ops.
[04:39] Omar: On pricing approvals, do you require a minimum commit term for Dedicated?
[04:44] Carlos: Yes, Dedicated usually involves a monthly or annual commit; the discounted unit rate applies to committed volumes. We can show break-even points in the spreadsheet.
[04:53] Lena: Can Redwood accept limited PO net-60 terms? That's our standard.
[04:57] Sarah: Net-60 is possible at enterprise tier; we'll note that and follow up with commercial.
[05:02] Priya: A couple of specific DPA asks: 1) clarify subprocessors list, 2) delete raw prompts on request within X days, and 3) add audit log retention limits.
[05:12] Sarah: We'll propose language that allows deletion on request with a standard notice window and an option for extended retention if needed for debugging, with customer approval.
[05:22] Mark: For KMS, what SLAs for key access and rotation do you have? We can't have a design that introduces single-point KMS outages.
[05:31] Carlos: We support key-rotation and HSM-backed KMS providers. In Private, you keep KMS in your control plane, so outages are your domain; Redwood will surface retries and fallback. We'll provide architectural diagrams.
[05:46] Lena: Anything we should prepare for the procurement board?
[05:49] Sarah: Yes: the redlined MSA/DPA, SOC2, the cost spreadsheet, example SLA matrix, and the short benchmark results. Those should give you what procurement expects.
[06:00] Priya: Ok. We'll look for the redline and confirm if any additional redlines are requested before 2026-05-11.
[06:06] Nina: I'll follow up with the technical invite and bookkeeping items.
[06:10] Sarah: Great. Recap of owners: Sarah sends MSA/DPA and SOC2, Carlos sends cost sheet and runs benchmark, Nina schedules the VPC run, Priya and Lena confirm procurement schedule. Anything else?
[06:23] Omar: One small point: can you include a short note on data egress estimates per 1M tokens? Helps our forecasting.
[06:30] Carlos: Will do. We'll include a per-million token egress estimate and breakdown by embedding vs generation.
[06:37] Sarah: Thanks everyone. We'll follow up and aim to be in time for your board.
[06:42] Lena: Thanks. Bye.
[06:44] Meeting end.
